text.autoconfig.YungsRoads-fabric-1_21.o: The distance between neighboring routing nodes, in blocks.
Lower values follow the terrain more closely, but are slower to generate.
How strongly routing is pulled toward the destination. 1.0 always finds the cheapest road.
Higher values generate faster, but roads may take slightly worse routes.
Place road blocks in the world. Turn off to see routes on the tuning screen's overlay without changing terrain.
yungsroads.setting.node_step_distance.de: The distance between neighboring nodes, in blocks. Lower values follow the terrain more closely, but are slower to generate.
yungsroads.setting.heuristic_weight.desc: How strongly routing is pulled toward the destination, by weighting the distance left in each node's search priority. 1 always finds the cheapest road. Higher values generate faster, but can give slightly costlier roads.
yungsroads.setting.jitter_amount.descrip: How far jitter may shift the road sideways, in blocks. Higher values make roads wavier.
yungsroads.setting.slope_weight.descript: How strongly roads avoid steep ground. Higher values make roads go around hills and mountains rather than over them. Steps steeper than Free Grade cost (1 + Slope Weight × (grade² - Free Grade²)) times as much as flat ones.
yungsroads.setting.free_grade.descriptio: The steepest grade that costs nothing extra to route over. Higher values let roads run straight over gentle rises instead of weaving around them, but weaken the pull toward switchbacks on hillsides. A 1-block rise over one node step is a grade of 0.125 at the default Node Step Distance.
yungsroads.setting.straighten_routes.des: Straighten each route after it's found, removing needless zigzags. A run of nodes is replaced by a straight line wherever that costs no more, stays within Max Grade, and doesn't cross water. Turn off to see routes as routing found them.
yungsroads.setting.max_grade.description: The steepest grade a road may have. Routing never crosses steeper terrain, and where the ground between nodes is steeper, the road cuts or tunnels through it. 0.5 climbs 1 block every 2 blocks, and 1 is a 45 degree slope.
yungsroads.setting.water_weight.descript: How strongly roads avoid crossing water. Higher values make roads detour further around rivers and lakes, or to a narrower crossing. Each bridge costs Water Weight extra per block of its run.
yungsroads.setting.max_bridge_length.des: The longest bridge a road may build, in blocks. Roads cross rivers and lakes only on straight bridges, so they go around wider water. 0 disables bridges. Oceans are never crossed.
yungsroads.setting.road_width.descriptio: How wide the road is where it's narrowest, in blocks. Its bridges and tunnels are as wide as the road leading onto them.
yungsroads.setting.width_variation.descr: How much wider the road gets in places, in blocks. Along the road, its width varies smoothly between Road Width and Road Width plus Width Variation. 0 keeps the road the same width all along.
yungsroads.setting.smoothing_radius.desc: How far along the road its height is averaged, in blocks. Higher values give gentler slopes, with more cutting and filling to level the ground. 0 follows the terrain.
yungsroads.setting.max_cut_depth.descrip: The deepest a road may cut into the ground above it to stay level, in blocks. Where the ground rises higher, the road rises with it, unless that would be steeper than Max Grade, in which case it tunnels through.
yungsroads.setting.max_fill_depth.descri: The deepest gap under a road that's filled with ground, in blocks. Deeper gaps, such as ravines and cave openings, are crossed on a land bridge instead.
yungsroads.setting.max_land_bridge_lengt: The longest dip in the terrain that a road crosses on a land bridge, in blocks. Shorter dips deeper than Max Fill Depth are bridged, and longer ones are followed down and back up. Ravines and carved caves always get a land bridge, since routing can't see them.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_edge_roug: How ragged the edges of land bridges are. 0 gives straight edges. Higher values move each edge block up to a block in or out.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_decay.des: How much of each land bridge's deck is missing, for a ruined look. Blocks are likelier to be missing toward the edges, and the center line is always kept. 0 keeps the whole deck.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_sag.descr: How far each land bridge's deck sags between its ends, as a fraction of its length. The sag is limited so the deck is never steeper than Max Grade. 0 gives straight decks.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_railing_d: How far the ground beside a land bridge must drop below its deck for that edge to get a railing, in blocks. Lower values put railings along more of each bridge.
yungsroads.setting.land_bridge_railing_c: The chance, in percent, that each edge block of a land bridge with a drop beside it gets a railing. 100 lines every such edge, and 0 places no railings.
yungsroads.glossary.node.definition: A point on the grid that roads are routed through. Neighboring nodes are Node Step Distance blocks apart.
yungsroads.glossary.step.definition: A move from a node to one of its 16 neighbors: the 8 around it, including diagonals, and the 8 a chess knight's move away, which allow smoother headings.
yungsroads.glossary.step_cost.definition: How much routing charges for one step. Routing picks the route with the lowest total cost, so costly terrain is avoided when a cheaper detour exists. A step across flat land costs 1 per block of its length, and steep ground or water make it cost more.
yungsroads.glossary.bridge.definition: A straight crossing over water, from a node on one bank to the first dry node on the other. Bridges can head the same ways as steps, and their length is measured between the two bank nodes, so the shortest possible bridge is twice Node Step Distance. Like steps, bridges can't be steeper than Max Grade. Their extra cost per block makes roads take the shortest crossing that's worth it over a detour.
yungsroads.glossary.run.definition: The horizontal length of a step or bridge, in blocks: Node Step Distance for a straight move to a neighbor, or 1.41 or 2.24 times that for a diagonal or knight's move.
yungsroads.glossary.grade.definition: How steep a step is: its change in height divided by its run (rise over run). 0 is flat, 0.5 climbs 1 block every 2 blocks, and 1 is a 45 degree slope. Over water, the height used is sea level.
yungsroads.glossary.water.definition: Ground below sea level, such as rivers and lakes. Steps never enter it, so roads only cross it on straight bridges at sea level. Oceans are never crossed.
yungsroads.glossary.search_priority.defi: Nodes are explored in order of search priority, lowest first, until the destination is reached.
yungsroads.glossary.cost_so_far.definiti: The total step cost of the cheapest known route from the start to a node.
yungsroads.glossary.distance_left.defini: The straight-line distance from a node to the destination, in blocks. Weighted by Heuristic Weight: at 1, routing always finds the cheapest road. Higher weights rush toward the destination, which generates faster but can give slightly costlier roads.
yungsroads.glossary.jitter.definition: A noise-based sideways shift applied to each node after routing, so roads look less straight. It doesn't affect cost.
yungsroads.glossary.land_bridge.definiti: A crossing over a hole or dip in the ground, such as a ravine or cave opening, built from bridge blocks at the height of the road on either side. Routing plans one over each dip deeper than Max Fill Depth and up to Max Land Bridge Length long. Ravines and carved caves, which routing can't see, get one wherever the road would be more than Max Fill Depth above the ground. Each land bridge extends a few blocks past its rims, and railings line its edges wherever the drop beside them is at least Land Bridge Railing Drop.
yungsroads.glossary.road_type.definition: A style of road, set by a file in a datapack: how it's routed, how it's shaped to the terrain, and what it's built from. Each road gets one road type, chosen by the biomes along it.
yungsroads.glossary.road_network.definit: A dimension's roads, set by a file in a datapack: the structures they connect, and the road types they can get. Dimensions without one have no roads.
yungsroads.glossary.variant.definition: One of several sets of settings in a road type. Roads of the type are split between its variants at random, in proportion to each variant's weight.
yungsroads.glossary.region.definition: A 4096 by 4096 block square of the world. Roads are generated a region at a time, the first time they're needed in or near it.
yungsroads.glossary.surface.definition: One of a road type's sets of road blocks, used where the ground under the road is one of its ground blocks. Each column of road uses the first surface that matches, and ground no surface matches gets a plain dirt path.
yungsroads.screen.title: YUNG's Roads Tuning
yungsroads.screen.singleplayer_only: YUNG's Roads' tuning screen only works in singleplayer.
yungsroads.screen.warning.title: YUNG's Roads: Use a Test World
yungsroads.screen.warning.text:
This is YUNG's Roads' tuning screen, for tuning how roads generate. It changes the world it's used in: applying settings regenerates the roads near you and re-places them in chunks that already generated, which can bury, cut through, or overwrite anything built near them.

Only use it in a test world, never in a world you care about.
yungsroads.screen.page.routing.descripti: Routing: where each road goes, and how it avoids steep ground and water.
yungsroads.screen.page.shaping.descripti: Shaping: how each road is fitted to the terrain: how wide it is, how its height is smoothed, where the ground is cut or filled, and where it crosses dips on land bridges.
yungsroads.screen.page.blocks.descriptio: Blocks: what each road is built from, on each kind of ground, and on its bridges and tunnels.
yungsroads.screen.road_type.tooltip:
The road type to start from. Apply uses your edits for it in this world, and once they're applied, you can export it as a road type file.
Only the road types this dimension's road network uses are listed, including its default road type (%s). Each road gets its road type from the biomes along it. Click a road on the map to see its road type, and why it got it, in the Inspect tab.
yungsroads.screen.variant.name: Variant
yungsroads.screen.variant.tooltip: The variant whose settings you're editing. Roads of this road type are split between its variants at random, in proportion to their weights.
yungsroads.screen.variant.only.tooltip: This road type has a single variant, so all its roads use these settings.
yungsroads.screen.baseline: Value in %s when this world loaded: %s (Reset restores it)
yungsroads.screen.no_network: This dimension has no road network, so it has no roads or road types to tune. The map says how to add one.
yungsroads.screen.global.note: Used by every road type. Saved to the mod's config file, not to a road type.
yungsroads.screen.view.note: These options only change what's drawn on the map and in the world. They take effect right away, with nothing to apply or save.
yungsroads.screen.global.place_roads.des: Place road blocks in the world. Turn off to see routes on the overlay without changing terrain.
yungsroads.screen.view.world_overlay.des: Draw each road's route as a line in the world, in the road's own color, with its bridges in white and its ends marked in green. Parts hidden behind terrain are drawn faintly through it.
yungsroads.screen.view.previous_roads.de: Draw the roads replaced by the last Apply or Undo in red, on the map and overlay, to compare them with the new roads.
yungsroads.screen.view.nodes.description: Mark each road's nodes in white, on the map and overlay, to see where routing placed them.
yungsroads.screen.view.region_borders.de: Draw the borders between regions on the map.
yungsroads.screen.view.terrain.descripti:
What's drawn under the map, one pixel per node.
Height: the ground's height, from green near sea level through tan to white on peaks, shaded so slopes stand out.
Slope: each spot's steepest grade, from green when flat to red at Max Grade.
Cost: each spot's step cost, as a multiple of flat land's, from green at 1x to red at 50x or more, on a log scale.
Water is light blue, and oceans, which roads never cross, are dark blue. Purple is steeper than Max Grade, so roads can't cross it. Slope and Cost use the road type you're editing, including changes you haven't applied.
yungsroads.screen.view.center_map.descri: Move the map back to where you are.
yungsroads.screen.apply.tooltip: Regenerate the roads within %s blocks of you with your changes on the Road Type and Global tabs, then place them in loaded chunks. If your changes only affect how roads are placed, such as their blocks or width, or Place roads, the roads are re-placed without regenerating them, which is much faster.
yungsroads.screen.revert.tooltip: Undo the last Apply, restoring the settings and roads from before it. Press again to redo it.
yungsroads.screen.reset.road_type.toolti: Reset the variant you're editing to the road type as this world loaded it. Press Apply to use it.
yungsroads.screen.reset.global.tooltip: Reset the global settings to their defaults. Press Apply to use them.
yungsroads.screen.unapplied: You have unapplied changes. Press Apply to preview them.
yungsroads.screen.copy_json.tooltip: Copy %s, as applied, to the clipboard as a road type file. Paste it into a datapack to add a new road type or replace this one. Help's Road networks section explains how.
yungsroads.screen.save_datapack.tooltip: Save %s, as applied, to this world's datapack %s. It replaces the road type in this world from the next time the world loads. The datapack can be copied into other worlds or a modpack.
yungsroads.screen.save_config.tooltip: Save the applied global settings to the mod's config file, used by every world.
yungsroads.screen.apply_first.road_type: Apply your changes to this road type first, so you export what you've previewed.
yungsroads.screen.apply_first.global: Apply your changes to the global settings first, so you save what you've previewed.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.surface.earlier: Try this surface before the one above it
yungsroads.screen.blocks.surface.later: Try this surface after the one below it
yungsroads.screen.blocks.surface.add.des: Add a surface, starting as a copy of the last one. Surfaces are tried in order: each column of road uses the first whose ground blocks include the ground under it.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.ground.descript: The ground blocks this surface replaces. Wherever the top block of the ground under the road is one of these, the road is built from this surface's path and fill blocks in its place. Block tags, such as #minecraft:dirt, match every block in them, including other mods' blocks. Each column of road uses the first surface that matches its ground block.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.path.descriptio: The blocks the road is made of on this surface, each with its chance.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.fill.descriptio: The blocks that build up the ground under the road where it's raised above it, and that replace the ground block it covers. Without them, the ground's own block is copied.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.fill.none_optio: No fill blocks: copy the ground's own block
yungsroads.screen.blocks.deck.descriptio: The blocks bridges over water and land bridges are built from.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.railings.descri: The railings along the edges of land bridges with a drop beside them. Fences, walls, panes, and bars connect to each other. Without them, land bridges have no railings.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.lining.descript: The blocks lining the walls and ceilings of tunnels. Without them, tunnels are bare, with only unstable blocks and fluids in their walls made solid.
yungsroads.screen.blocks.lining.none_opt: No lining: leave tunnel walls bare
yungsroads.blocks.no_rows: No blocks yet. Add one below.
yungsroads.blocks.no_rows.weighted: Only the default block. Add blocks to mix in.
yungsroads.blocks.error.chance: Enter a chance from 0 to 100 for %s.
yungsroads.blocks.error.total: The chances add up to %s%%, more than 100%%.
yungsroads.screen.inspect.tooltip: Show or hide details of a spot on the map. Click the map to pin a spot.
yungsroads.screen.invalid: Fix the values shown in red before applying (%s)
yungsroads.screen.copied: Copied road type %s to the clipboard
yungsroads.status.reverted: Undid the last Apply. Press Undo again to redo it.
yungsroads.status.saved_road_type: Saved road type %s to this world's datapack %s. It's used from the next time the world loads.
yungsroads.status.save_road_type_failed: Unable to save the road type: %s
yungsroads.status.saved_config: Saved the global settings to the config file.
yungsroads.status.save_config_failed: Unable to save the global settings: %s

yungsroads.formula.max_grade: Steps steeper than grade %s are never taken
yungsroads.formula.max_bridge_length: Bridges are at most %s blocks long
yungsroads.formula.search_priority: Search priority = cost so far + %s × distance left

yungsroads.formula.global.title: Global formulas

yungsroads.map.bridge_only: Only crossed by straight bridges, up to %s blocks long
yungsroads.map.step_cost: Steepest step cost: run × (1 + %s × max(0, %s² - %s²)) = run × %s
yungsroads.map.node: Node cost so far: %s, weighted distance left: %s, search priority: %s
yungsroads.map.no_network.text:
This dimension has no road network, so it has no roads.
To give it roads, add this file to a datapack, then reload the world:

yungsroads.map.network.title: Road network for %s
yungsroads.map.network.reload: As loaded with the world. Edit the datapack files and reload the world to change it. The Help tab explains how.
yungsroads.map.teleport: Right-click the map to teleport there.
yungsroads.inspect.title: Inspect
yungsroads.inspect.how: Hover the map to see details of any spot here. Click the map to pin a spot, so it stays here while you change settings. Click the pin again to unpin it.
yungsroads.inspect.group.terrain.descrip: The ground at this spot, as routing samples it, whatever the settings.
yungsroads.inspect.group.edits.descripti: What routing would charge to cross this spot with the road type you're editing, including changes you haven't applied.
yungsroads.inspect.group.world.descripti: Roads as they're generated now, which Apply regenerates with your edits, and this dimension's road network.
yungsroads.inspect.not_sampled: The terrain here hasn't been sampled yet. Zoom the map in over it, or wait a moment.
yungsroads.inspect.no_road: No road passes near this spot.
yungsroads.help.title: Help
yungsroads.help.overview.title: About this screen
yungsroads.help.overview.text:
This tool allows you to tune the roads from YUNG's Roads in real time. On the Road Type tab, pick an existing road type to start from and edit its settings as desired. Press Apply to regenerate the roads near you with them, then export the tuned road type with Copy JSON or Save to Datapack.
When you press Apply, it re-places roads in chunks that have already generated, which can overwrite anything built near them.
§4USE A TEST WORLD!§r
yungsroads.help.road_types.title: Road types
yungsroads.help.road_types.text:
Every road has a road type, which sets how it's routed, how it's shaped to the terrain, and what it's built from. Road types are datapack files in data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_type, so datapacks can add their own or override the ones the mod ships with.
Each road's road type is chosen by the biomes along it. The biome is sampled every 64 blocks along the straight line between the road's ends, and each sample votes for the road types in the dimension's road network that select its biome. The road type with the most votes wins.
Selection: the biomes a road type is chosen for, as a biome, a list of biomes, or a biome tag.
Priority: decides between road types whose biomes overlap. In a biome that several road types select, only those with the highest priority get its vote. A tie in votes also goes to the higher priority.
Default: the road network's default road type gets the vote of every sample that none of its road types select. The Overworld's is yungsroads:default.
Variants: a road type can have several variants, each with its own settings. Roads of the road type are split between them at random, in proportion to each variant's weight. A variant with weight 3 gets three times as many roads as one with weight 1.
Click a road on the map to see its road type and the votes that chose it in the Inspect tab.
yungsroads.help.road_networks.title: Road networks
yungsroads.help.road_networks.text:
Each dimension's roads are set by its road network, a datapack file named after the dimension: data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_network/<dimension>.json, such as data/minecraft/yungsroads/road_network/overworld.json. Dimensions without one have no roads. The Inspect tab shows this dimension's road network.
structures: the structures its roads connect, as a structure, a list of structures, or a structure tag.
road_types: the road types its roads can get, as a road type, a list of road types, or a road type tag. Only these are listed on this screen. The Overworld's are the tag #yungsroads:overworld, so a datapack can add a road type to the Overworld with the tag file data/yungsroads/tags/yungsroads/road_type/overworld.json, without replacing its road network.
default_road_type: the road type that gets the vote of every sample that none of the network's road types select.
Adding a road type: on the Road Type tab, pick an existing road type to start from, tune it, press Apply, then press Copy JSON. Paste it into a new file data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_type/<name>.json in a datapack, and change its selection to the biomes it's for. Then add <namespace>:<name> to the road types of each road network that should use it, such as with the tag file {"values": ["<namespace>:<name>"]}. Road types and road networks only load with the world, not with /reload, so reload the world, then tune the new road type here.
yungsroads.help.routing.title: Routing
yungsroads.help.routing.text: Routing finds where each road goes. It searches a grid of nodes for the route with the lowest total step cost, so roads avoid steep ground and water when a cheaper detour exists. These settings belong to the road type you're editing.
yungsroads.help.shaping.title: Shaping
yungsroads.help.shaping.text: Shaping fits a routed road to the terrain: how wide it is, how its height is smoothed, where the ground is cut or filled, and where it crosses dips on land bridges or bores through hills in tunnels. These settings belong to the road type you're editing.
yungsroads.help.blocks.title: Blocks
yungsroads.help.blocks.text:
The Blocks page sets what the road type you're editing is built from. Click a list of blocks to edit it in a dialog, where blocks are typed as ids, such as dirt_path or oak_slab[type=top], with suggestions as you type.
Road surface: the road's blocks over each kind of ground. Each column of road uses the first surface whose ground blocks include the ground under it, so put more specific surfaces first. Ground that no surface lists gets a plain dirt path. Ground blocks can be block tags, such as #minecraft:dirt, which also match other mods' blocks.
Path and fill: mixes of blocks, each with a chance, and a default block for the rest. Fill builds up the ground under a raised road. Without it, the ground's own block is copied.
Bridges: the deck blocks of bridges over water and land bridges, and the railings along land bridges with a drop beside them.
Tunnels: the blocks lining tunnel walls and ceilings.
Changes that only affect how roads are placed, such as blocks and Road Width, re-place the roads when you press Apply without regenerating them, so they're quick to try.
yungsroads.help.global.title: Global
yungsroads.help.global.text: Global settings apply to every road type, and are saved to the mod's config file rather than to a road type. Like road type settings, they're applied with the Apply button, then saved with Save to Config File. Changing only Place roads re-places roads without regenerating them.
yungsroads.help.view.title: View
yungsroads.help.view.text:
View options only change what's drawn on the map and in the world, and take effect right away. Nothing here changes the roads.
On the map, drag to pan, scroll to zoom, and right-click to teleport. The Inspect tab, beside the Help tab, describes the spot under the cursor: its terrain, the costs routing sees there, and the nearest road with its road type. Click the map to pin a spot, so the tab keeps showing it while you change settings, and click the pin again to unpin it.
yungsroads.help.saving.title: Applying and saving
yungsroads.help.saving.text:
Apply: regenerates the roads within %s blocks of you with your changes on the Road Type and Global tabs, then re-places them in loaded chunks. Roads further away keep their old shape until they're regenerated. Changes that only affect how roads are placed, such as blocks and Road Width, just re-place the roads, which is much faster.
Undo: restores the settings and roads from before the last Apply. Press it again to redo it.
Reset: on the Road Type tab, resets the variant you're editing to the road type as this world loaded it. On the Global tab, resets the global settings to their defaults. Press Apply to use them.
Values and road types you've edited are marked in yellow, and the panel says when you have changes you haven't applied. The export and save buttons only work once your changes are applied, so what you save is what you've previewed.
Copy JSON: copies the road type you're editing to the clipboard, as a road type file for a datapack. Use it to add a new road type, as described under Road networks.
Save to Datapack: saves the road type you're editing to a datapack in this world's datapacks folder, named yungsroads_tuned, replacing the road type in this world from the next time it loads. The datapack includes a README describing every setting, and can be copied into other worlds or a modpack.
Save to Config File: saves the global settings to the mod's config file, used by every world.
yungsroads.help.glossary.title: Glossary
yungsroads.docs.title: Road types tuned with YUNG's Roads
yungsroads.docs.intro: This datapack holds road types changed on YUNG's Roads' tuning screen. Each file in data/<namespace>/yungsroads/road_type overrides the road type with the same id, or adds a new one. To use them in another world, copy this folder into that world's datapacks folder, or add it to a modpack.
yungsroads.docs.choosing.title: How road types are chosen
yungsroads.docs.format.title: File format
yungsroads.docs.format.text: A road type has an optional selection, and either one set of settings or a list of weighted variants:
yungsroads.docs.settings.title: Settings
yungsroads.docs.settings.text: Each setting that's left out takes its default value. Unknown setting names are errors, so a misspelled setting is reported in the log rather than ignored.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.title: Blocks
yungsroads.docs.blocks.surfaces: The road's blocks over each kind of ground. Each column of the road uses the first surface that matches the ground there.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.target_blocks: The ground blocks the surface replaces. Wherever the top block of the ground under the road is one of these, the road is built from this surface's blocks in its place. Each is a block id, or a block tag starting with #, such as #minecraft:dirt, which also matches blocks other mods add to the tag.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.path_blockstates: The blocks the road is made of.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.fill_blockstates: Optional. The blocks that build up the ground under a road raised above it. Without it, the ground's own block is copied.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.bridge_blockstate: The blocks bridges over water and land bridges are built from.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.bridge_railing_bl: Optional. The railings along the edges of land bridges with a drop beside them. Fences, walls, panes, and bars connect to each other. Without it, land bridges have no railings.
yungsroads.docs.blocks.tunnel_lining_blo: Optional. The blocks lining the walls and ceilings of tunnels. Without it, tunnels are bare, with only unstable blocks and fluids in their walls made solid.
yungsroads.docs.global.title: Global settings
yungsroads.docs.global.text: Node Step Distance and Heuristic Weight apply to every road type, so they're in the mod's config file instead of a road type's file.
